f21f0bb7a233035255d30dd651cd5471.text: Williams Lake Social Collective hosted their first healthcare mixers on Saturday, Nov. 21 bringing together 28 healthcare professionals to build community connections. The Saturday, Nov. 21 gathering is part of an effort to retain local health-care workers by helping them build connections and feel more at home in the community. Jerusha Alvares, a speech-language pathologist, and Ashleigh Cire, an optometrist, lead the Williams Lake Social Collective, which organizes events to help newcomers meet people and get involved in the community. Participants get creative during an art activity at the Williams Lake Social Collective's health-care mixer. The Williams Lake Social Collective raised more than $800 for future events aimed at helping people build connections in the community. Twenty-eight healthcare professionals from across Williams Lake’s healthcare community gathered at the Osprey Nest on Saturday, Nov. 21, for the Williams Lake Social Collective’s first healthcare mixer. The event brought together optometrists, occupational therapists, pedorthists, dentists, respiratory therapists and nurses. The two organizers, Ashleigh Cire and Jerusha Alvares, who both work in healthcare, said they wanted to give people in the field a chance to meet outside work and build connections in Williams Lake. The organizers said recruitment and retention were on their minds when they planned the mixer. In an email to the Tribune, they pointed to emergency department closures during staffing shortages as an example of how gaps in staffing can affect the wider community. “We know how important it is to have a strong healthcare team within the community to support the health and wellbeing of those who live within it,” said Alvares. 3cc11baa70f11b295e3395ae72d3f6fa.text: WL Kitty Spay founder Cassidy Porter and vice president Crystal Sheridan were at Cariboo Corner on Saturday, Nov. 21 for their first annual Pet Vendor Market. Collecting donations in Williams Lake to assist feline owners cover the costs for spaying and neutering is how Cassidy Porter helps the furry animals she is severely allergic to. It has just been over two years since Porter founded the non-profit WL Kitty Spay that hosted its first Pet Vendor Market on Saturday, Nov. 21 at Cariboo Corner. Wearing a holiday cat themed pullover sweater Porter was joined with vice president Crystal Sheridan at the afternoon event where people could purchase entries for one of three Christmas baskets and learn more about WL Kitty Spay. Also available were pet dishes donated by Save-On-Foods and harnesses and collars provided by pet stores in the Lower Mainland. “We just wanted a chance to raise money for our spay and neuter program, and thought we would try something different and tailor it to pet themed items for the the public,” Porter said of the Pet Market that coincided with several holiday craft markets. Since launching WL Kitty Spay, more than 170 cats have been spayed or neutered through providing financial support for the costs of the procedure in addition to a microchip and cone collar. With 30 cats on their waitlist and donations having slowed down for a bit, Porter said they had to currently suspend any additions to the list. She is hopeful, however, with the holiday season that donations will increase and they’ll be able to open up their waitlist again in the New Year. “Even with a double income household, times are tough right now and everything is really expensive,” she added. “It’ s expensive to fix your animals, and the cat overpopulation is pretty extreme right now so we just want to do what we can to help.” In a November 2026 news release, the BC SPCA stated pet overpopulation has been an increasing concern across the province, especially where cats may roam

8f5ac0698ce9cbc0be75a679a3f65d1b.text: Stephanie Higginson has been elected MLA for Ladysmith Oceanside following a judicial recount of the vote. Stephanie Higginson has finally been confirmed as MLA for Ladysmith Oceanside, following a judicial recount. The final results for the electoral district totalled 14,352 for Higginson of the BC NDP (44.4 per cent of the vote), narrowly defeating Kris McNichol of the Conservative Party, who garnered 14,305 votes, or 44.25 per cent of the vote, according to Elections BC. Charlene Smylie of the BC Green Party had 3,617 votes, or 11.19 per cent. There were 51 “rejected ballots”, according to Elections BC. “It felt really good to know that we’d come to an end and the riding and the constituency had officially elected me. It comes with a lot of responsibility and also a big honour. I’m just really thrilled to be back in the position,” Higginson said. Higginson and McNichol went into the judicial recount just 13 votes apart, which widened to 47 when the recount concluded. “Congratulations to Stephanie. She ran a good campaign. I thought we ran a good campaign. Smylie ran a good campaign,” McNichol said, and noted the riding totalled the most votes in B.C. in the provincial election. “We made some inroads, obviously, and when you look at all of British Columbia, they spoke. They wanted change. Apparently Ladysmith Oceanside didn’t want the change needed, but we sure gave it a run.” He added that nothing will change for him, as a businessman, and he is back to running his businesses, rather than heading to Victoria. “We move forward. It was a long road to get here,” McNichol said, and added he is grateful to his volunteers, supporters and campaign team: “They’re the ones I’m doing this for”. Higginson said that during the month-long process, she tried to keep things in perspective, recognizing that she would have her family and her health, regardless of the final election outcome. “The uncertainty of how you’re going to be spending your time, it was getting a bit long

f6e206e637c3689351743bc3c6060f0a.text: Two black bear cubs are shown in this photo shared by Wild Wise Society. Two black bear cubs have been struck and killed by a vehicle along the Trans-Canada Highway near Goldstream Park. The BC Conservation Officer Service (BCCOS) confirmed they received a report Monday morning (Nov. 23). “Conservation officers responded to assess and address any immediate public safety concerns along this busy stretch of highway,” said a BCCOS statement. “Two cubs were located deceased.” Emcon Services, the contractor responsible for provincial highway maintenance, confirmed they were called to collect the two bears. A spokesperson said the carcasses were “disposed of appropriately.” Sooke-based wildlife organization Wild Wise said it was “devastated” to hear of the incident. They said the death of the two cubs serves as a reminder of how important it is to remain vigilant when driving through areas where wildlife may be present. “Please slow down, watch for wildlife near roadways, and be especially attentive during periods of low visibility,” they said in a social media post. To avoid bear-vehicle collisions, the Wildlife Collision Prevention Program – which aims to make B.C.’s highways safer for both people and wildlife through education and awareness – drivers should drive defensively, concentrating on the road at all times. Drivers should watch the sides of the road for wildlife attempting to cross, especially where visibility is poor, using extra caution at night. In the event of a collision, the organization advises drivers to always call BCCOS on 1-877-952-7277 if there is an injured animal to report. “A wounded animal can be very dangerous,” they say. “You are not required to put an injured animal out of its misery.” If there is damage over $1,000, any human injuries, or the animal carcass is not safe to be moved and presents an urgent highway safety issue, WCPP says to call the RCMP. ad1006f112a8f00566e1c72bdcc60c81.text: A total of 373 lives were remembered during this year's Transgender Day of Remembrance, with two victims from Vancouver. Nanaimo community members and allies solemnly packed Sands Funeral Chapel on Friday, mourning the lives lost over the past year on Transgender Day of Remembrance. Transgender Day of Remembrance began in 1999 to remember the lives of transgender people whose lives were taken to anti-trans violence. A total of 373 names were recognized this year who died from suicide or violence, in addition to two names from cancer and one from HIV. Five names come from Canada, including two from Vancouver. During the Nanaimo vigil held on Nov. 20, Nathan Rokeby, a transgender 15-year-old boy, read a poem in one of the past victim’s memory. He stated that as a trans youth, he fears each election as some provincial governments institute laws targeting trans people. “I can’t be expected to be unaffected as I watch adults I’m supposed to look up to create laws with the intent to silence me and the result to kill me. I am trans, I am proud of it, but I am also a kid. I am the boy who wishes I could have a say, I am the child who wants to grow up,” he said. “Let me love, let me live, let me grow up like so many of us didn’t.” Lauren Semple, president of the Nanaimo Pride Society, said that while over 300 names were recorded this year, she knows with “devastating certainty” that the numbers are likely higher, but the victims were denied their trans identity in death. “We are living through a time of unprecedented legislative and physical hostility,” she said. Semple cited the number of bills targeting trans people in the United States alone, which, according to Trans Legislation Tracker, totalled 1,022 bills in 2025, 126 passing. “The global impact is equally staggering. 305e2b4d9181ca6636a308a783cdb43a.text: A police laser reading showing a blue BMW that was allegedly going 208 km/h in a 90 zone on B.C.'s Sea to Sky Highway. A 22-year-old California man was allegedly caught going 118 kilometres an hour over the posted speed limit on the Sea to Sky Highway. A B.C. Highway Patrol officer saw a southbound blue BMW driving “much faster” than other traffic on Highway 99 near Squamish on Nov. 1 around 5:10 p.m., according to a news release from police on Tuesday (Nov. 24). The officer used his police laser and got a speed reading of 208 km/h in a 90 zone, the release says. “Even by the standards of the Sea to Sky Highway, this is a terribly dangerous speed,” Sgt. Michael McLaughlin said. “Visitors to B.C. are expected to understand and obey our traffic laws. You will not ‘get a break’ just to avoid the inconvenience of losing your vehicle and interrupting your vacation plans.” The driver was issued a $483-fine for excessive speed over 60 km/h, as well as the cost of a tow truck and a seven-day impound. “No matter whether it’s locals or visitors, treating the Sea to Sky like the autobahn has got to stop. There is a direct correlation between dangerous driving and deadly collisions that shut this highway down for hours at a time,” McLaughlin said.

ce583d7cfa9388385315ff51e949dc3a.text: Conservative candidate Kristina Loewen won the Kelowna Centre riding by 132 votes on election night, Oct. 24, 2026. Conservative Party of BC candidate Kristina Loewen has won Kelowna Centre following a judicial recount, widening her margin over the BC NDP’s Loyal Wooldridge, to 46 votes. In a Facebook post, Loewen announced that the recount was complete. Elections BC posted the results on its website Tuesday (Nov. 23) afternoon, confirming the totals. “The Kelowna Centre recount is done!!! I’ve now won with a margin of 46 votes (up from 43)!!!!” Loewen wrote on Facebook. “I’m ready to be able to fully move forward in my role as an MLA representing Kelowna Centre – as well as in my new role as Minister of Children and Family Development.” Loewen also thanked Wooldridge and OneBC candidate Bill Desrossier for contesting the seat. Following election night on Oct. 24, Loewen held a lead of 132 to 137 votes over Wooldridge before mail-in, absentee, and telephone ballots were counted during Elections BC’s final count between Nov. 6-8. Once those ballots were factored in, Loewen’s advantage narrowed to 43 votes—11,689 votes to Wooldridge’s 11,646 votes. Because the margin fell below Election BC’s automatic judicial recount threshold of one-500th of total ballots cast (48 votes in Kelowna Centre), the riding headed back to a judicial recount which started Nov. 23. The finish echoed the 2024 provincial election where Loewen and Wooldridge also battled down to the wire, and a judicial recount was also needed.

1342e4a0399b40a9728a00b9f6f640b5.text: Photo of weapons seized from the last 2 months of pro-active enforcement in Prince George, British Columbia. The Prince George RCMP has seized a significant cache of weapons during ongoing proactive enforcement efforts targeting public safety concerns in the downtown core. According to an RCMP press release, the seizures were carried out by the RCMP’s Problem Oriented Policing (POP) Unit and Downtown Safety Unit (DSU) as part of targeted initiatives addressing crime and disorder. Mounties said among the items seized was a large assortment of edged and improvised weapons, pellet and replica-style firearms, batons, brass knuckles and a crossbow with bolts. “The work of our Problem Oriented Policing and Downtown Safety teams continues to have a direct impact on community safety,” Sgt. Craig Douglass of the Prince George RCMP said. “The removal of these weapons reduces the potential for violence and demonstrates our commitment to proactive policing in areas where residents and businesses have identified safety concerns.” Police said the seizures are the result of ongoing collaboration between specialized enforcement teams focused on repeat offenders, weapon possession and crime trends affecting the downtown area. The Prince George RCMP said it remains committed to working with community partners to improve public safety and maintain a safe environment for residents, visitors and businesses.

7c2eb29e73294c4e1e9c2f9f34c95c44.text: A copper exploration company building a portfolio of high potential projects in B.C. and Western Australia has acquired a project adjacent to the Mount Polley mine northeast of Williams Lake near Likely. According to a news release Osiris Copper Corp. (Osiris One Metals Ltd.) entered into a binding Nov. 12 letter of intent to acquire the Miracle Gold Project that comprises two mineral claims covering approximately 6,300 hectares immediately west of Imperial Metals’ Mount Polley mine in the Quesnel Terrane. The Miracle Gold project is additionally located approximately 35 kilometres west of Canada’s second largest open pit copper mine, Trekor Metals’ Gibraltar Mine. It is covered by a B.C. exploration permit, valid to 2031, which authorises up to 50 surface drilling sites. “Miracle represents an attractive opportunity to advance a sizeable copper gold exploration property within one of British Columbia’s most established porphyry copper districts,” stated Osiris One Metals CEO Sreenath Didugu. “The project’s proximity to the Mount Polley and Gibraltar mines provides an important regional context. Particularly given the presence of mapped intrusive rocks, brecciation, alteration and historical copper anomalies across the property which have not yet been systematically followed up through a comprehensive modern exploration programme.” Osiris Copper Corp’s immediate focus according to Didugu will be on integrating the historical work with the exploration program completed this month to better understand the intrusive systems and refine priority targets. He said they believe the Miracle Gold Project has great geological potential, and its addition further strengthens Osiris’ portfolio of copper exploration assets in B.C. In June, Vancouver-based exploration company Inomin Mines Inc. announced the largest single exploration investment of $2.3 million at the Beaver-Lynx polymetallic project that is adjacent to the Gibraltar Mine.

An organization called the ARC Foundation created and administered the resources but lost its contract with the government last summer, effectively ending SOGI as an active program. It is now up to individual school districts whether to continue using SOGI resources. Doerkson says the education minister will work with districts to remove the materials from individual classrooms. “We’ve asked for it to be removed from the room, so if it’s not, they’re not just going to get pushback from the parents; they’re going to get pushback from me as well,” he said. B.C. Teachers’ Federation President Carole Gordon said this decision is “rooted in misinformation,” questioning what this will mean in practice and what specific resources will be removed. She also sought to reiterate that gender-diverse children need support in school. “Every child deserves to walk through the doors of their school feeling comfortable in who they are, knowing they have friends and adults in their corner,” Gordon said in a written statement. “We’ll always stand up for that.” Interim NDP Leader Jennifer Whiteside wants to know what those resources will be replaced with, noting SOGI’s success in reducing bullying. “That’s a serious question that both vulnerable youth and families and educators are going to want to understand,” she said. “What exactly is the plan?” B.C. 7f970d14a981cfe100c20958d95d2399.text: Police are keeping quiet about a chase through downtown Penticton. RCMP are keeping quiet about a recent video documenting part of a police chase through downtown Penticton. The video, posted to Instagram by Michelle Prystay, shows five police cruisers in pursuit of a white pickup truck along Nanaimo Avenue on Nov. 24. The pickup truck, with what appears to be a pair of ATVs strapped down in the bed, drives through the CIBC parking lot off Nanaimo Square, over the concrete parking stops and back into the street. As it drives over the concrete, the vehicle’s passenger falls out of the truck, and attempts to sprint down the road, stumbling into a faceplant in the middle of the intersection with Martin Street, before getting up and continuing to run down Nanaimo. The video does not show whether the individuals were taken into custody. The Penticton Western News reached out to the RCMP for comment, and the RCMP declined to share any information. “We are actively investigating this incident, and at this time are unable to provide any information to protect the integrity of our investigation,” said Const. Olivier Nielis, media relations officer with the RCMP. The video is titled GTA Penticton, referring to massively successful Grand Theft Auto video game franchise that saw its most recent release, GTA6, debut to millions of sales and high critical praise on Nov. 19.

One of Premier Lorne Doerkson’s first acts since his cabinet was sworn in on Friday is to order Public Service head Kim Henderson to begin implementing a return-to-office plan for government workers. “The public servants who can work from the office will be back at it five days a week,” he said Wednesday (Nov. 25). Henderson is instructed to begin a phased return by reviewing existing remote work arrangements. Doerkson argues in-person collaboration will mean a more productive work environment. “This is about better service to British Columbians; people in the same room collaborate better, new employees get mentored by people who have been around, and ministries solve problems together,” he said. The premier also says this is a fairness issue, pointing out that many frontline government workers can’t work from home. “Nurses, doctors, teachers, correctional workers, and the people delivering frontline services show up in person every single day,” he said. “I think it’s reasonable to ask for people in our offices to do the same.” Doerkson says he’s been working in a near-empty office near the legislature, and still has no idea how many offices around the province are rented out but sit idle and under-utilized. B.C. General Employees’ Union President Paul Finch says he still has not met with the incoming government on this issue. He wants a better understanding of the government’s intentions and to get a chance to bring forward his members’ perspectives. 4c67c2ef6dda2084233f52d65321dc63.text: Japanese national arrested in Ontario in connection with B.C. aggravated assault | Williams Lake Tribune Japanese national arrested in Ontario in connection with B.C. aggravated assault A Vancouver Police Department cruiser parked on Cordova Street on July 23, 2025. A suspect who was wanted on a Canada-wide warrant for aggravated assault in B.C. was arrested in Ontario recently. Yuki Saito, 20, was charged in October with aggravated assault stemming from an incident on April 25, 2025 when an unhoused man was allegedly assaulted and beaten in Stanley Park to the point of unconsciousness, according to a news release from Vancouver police Wednesday (Nov. 25). Saito was released on conditions following his arrest, but he failed to attend a scheduled court appearance. Police said that despite extensive efforts to locate Saito, investigators were unable to find him through “traditional investigative methods.” The suspect is a Japanese national on a student visa, Sgt. Adam Donaldson said. Investigator were given judicial authority to track a cellular device believed to be associated with Saito. On Friday (Nov. 20), investigators learned the suspect was in the York region of Ontario. Vancouver officers worked with York Regional Police, who located and arrested Saito without incident. Saito remains in custody and is expected to be returned to B.C.

174d5d24c0e101a56a31927150645fca.text: A 17-year-old was caught going almost 100 kilometres per hour over the speed limit in Maple Ridge over the weekend. The teen was stopped by the Maple Ridge RCMP Road Safety Target Team at around 9 p.m. Sunday evening going 175km/h in a 80km/h zone in the 27200 block of Lougheed Highway. A tier two excessive speeding ticket was handed to the driver for driving more than double the speed limit and police had their vehicle towed and impounded for seven days. “Needless to say, officers also had quite the conversation with this young person who will likely face a driving prohibition from the BC Superintendent of Motor Vehicles,” said Maple Ridge RCMP online. “Don’t let an open road be an invitation to test your vehicle’s speedometer. Slow down and drive safely, especially during this time of year with changing weather conditions,” RCMP added.
